questions.statement: She said that she ___ tired. Choose the correct reported form.
questions.context: A student repeats what her friend said about feeling tired.

options.text: was
options.feedback: Was is correct: the present am backshifts to the past when the reporting verb said is in the past.

options.text: is
options.feedback: Is keeps the present tense and breaks the backshift that reported speech requires.

options.text: were
options.feedback: Were would need a plural subject, but the reported subject she is singular.

options.text: be
options.feedback: Be is the bare infinitive and cannot carry the past tense of the report.

questions.explanation:
Because the reporting verb said is past, am backshifts to was, so the report reads she said that she was tired.

questions.statement: He said that he ___ in Madrid. Choose the correct reported form.
questions.context: A boy tells his mother what his friend said about his home city.

options.text: lives
options.feedback: Lives stays in the present and does not follow the backshift rule.

options.text: lived
options.feedback: Lived is correct: the present simple live backshifts to the past simple after said.

options.text: live
options.feedback: Live is the plural present form and also keeps the wrong tense.

options.text: living
options.feedback: Living is a participle and cannot be the finite verb of the clause.

questions.explanation:
The present simple live becomes the past simple lived because the reporting verb is past.

questions.statement: They said that they ___ English. Choose the correct reported form.
questions.context: Two students report what their classmates announced before lunch.

options.text: are studying
options.feedback: Are studying keeps the present continuous, which the backshift rule changes.

options.text: studied
options.feedback: Studied changes the progressive aspect into the simple past, losing the idea of an action in progress.

options.text: were studying
options.feedback: Were studying is correct: the present continuous backshifts to the past continuous.

options.text: study
options.feedback: Study is the present simple and does not show the past report.

questions.explanation:
In reported speech the present continuous are studying becomes the past continuous were studying.

questions.statement: She said that she ___ swim very well. Choose the correct reported form.
questions.context: A girl repeats a skill her cousin mentioned during a call.

options.text: can
options.feedback: Can keeps the present modal and ignores the backshift.

options.text: can to
options.feedback: Can to is wrong because can never takes the particle to.

options.text: could to
options.feedback: Could to is wrong because a modal verb is followed by the bare infinitive.

options.text: could
options.feedback: Could is correct: the modal can backshifts to could in reported speech.

questions.explanation:
The modal can has no third form, so it backshifts to could after a past reporting verb.

questions.statement: He said that he would call me ___. Choose the correct time expression.
questions.context: A man repeats a promise his colleague made about a phone call.

options.text: the next day
options.feedback: The next day is correct: the adverb tomorrow shifts to the next day in reported speech.

options.text: tomorrow
options.feedback: Tomorrow keeps the original viewpoint and is not adjusted for the report.

options.text: today
options.feedback: Today points to the day of the report, not to the day after the original words.

options.text: yesterday
options.feedback: Yesterday points backwards and reverses the meaning of tomorrow.

questions.explanation:
When tomorrow is reported from a later day, it becomes the next day, and you becomes me.

questions.statement: She said that she had bought a new phone ___. Choose the correct time expression.
questions.context: A woman repeats a purchase her sister described after the weekend.

options.text: yesterday
options.feedback: Yesterday keeps the original day and does not match the past perfect report.

options.text: the day before
options.feedback: The day before is correct: yesterday shifts backwards to the day before in reported speech.

options.text: the next day
options.feedback: The next day points forward and reverses the meaning of yesterday.

options.text: now
options.feedback: Now is a present adverb and cannot replace a past day.

questions.explanation:
The past simple bought becomes had bought, and yesterday shifts to the day before.

questions.statement: The boss told me that I ___ finish the report. Choose the correct reported form.
questions.context: A boss gives an instruction that an employee later repeats.

options.text: must
options.feedback: Must keeps the present obligation and does not follow the backshift.

options.text: must to
options.feedback: Must to is wrong because a modal verb never takes the particle to.

options.text: had to
options.feedback: Had to is correct: the modal must backshifts to had to in a past report.

options.text: have to
options.feedback: Have to keeps the present tense, which the past report changes.

questions.explanation:
For an obligation reported in the past, must becomes had to because must has no past form.

questions.statement: He said that he ___ that film twice. Choose the correct reported form.
questions.context: A fan repeats what an actor said about a film.

options.text: has seen
options.feedback: Has seen keeps the present perfect and ignores the backshift.

options.text: saw
options.feedback: Saw is the simple past and loses the earlier-perfect meaning of the original.

options.text: seen
options.feedback: Seen is only the past participle and cannot stand alone as the finite verb.

options.text: had seen
options.feedback: Had seen is correct: the present perfect have seen backshifts to the past perfect.

questions.explanation:
The present perfect have seen becomes the past perfect had seen after the reporting verb said.

questions.statement: Marta said that ___ parents were travelling to Rome. Choose the correct possessive.
questions.context: A girl reports what a classmate said about her family trip.

options.text: her
options.feedback: Her is correct: the possessive my shifts to her when a third person reports the words of Marta.

options.text: my
options.feedback: My would keep Marta speaking in her own voice, which the report does not.

options.text: his
options.feedback: His refers to a male owner, but the speaker Marta is female.

options.text: their
options.feedback: Their refers to a plural owner, while Marta alone owns the parents in the report.

questions.explanation:
In reported speech the possessive pronoun my changes to her to match the third person subject.

questions.statement: The teacher ___ me that he was busy. Choose the correct reporting verb.
questions.context: A student repeats a message that a teacher gave him.

options.text: said
options.feedback: Said cannot take the object me directly; the correct form would be said to me.

options.text: told
options.feedback: Told is correct: the reporting verb told takes a personal object, so told me is right.

options.text: spoke
options.feedback: Spoke is not used to report a statement; it describes the act of speaking.

options.text: talked
options.feedback: Talked needs the preposition to before a person, as in talked to me.

questions.explanation:
Reported statements use tell plus a person or say plus to a person, so told me is correct here.

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the statement I am reading a book now?
questions.context: A student chooses the best reported version of a friend's words.

options.text: She said she is reading a book now.
options.feedback: Is reading keeps the present continuous and now stays in the present, so no backshift happens.

options.text: She said she was reading a book now.
options.feedback: Was reading is right but now must become then in the reported version.

options.text: She said she was reading a book then.
options.feedback: Was reading is correct, and now becomes then because the report is made later.

options.text: She said she read a book then.
options.feedback: Read is the simple past and loses the progressive meaning of the original.

questions.explanation:
The present continuous am reading backshifts to was reading, and the adverb now shifts to then.

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the statement The sun rises in the east?
questions.context: A teacher quotes a scientific fact and a student reports it.

options.text: The teacher said that the sun rose in the east.
options.feedback: Rose would suggest the fact was true only in the past, which is wrong for a general truth.

options.text: The teacher said that the sun had risen in the east.
options.feedback: Had risen adds a past perfect that a timeless fact does not need.

options.text: The teacher said the sun rise in the east.
options.feedback: Rise is the plural form and does not agree with the singular subject the sun.

options.text: The teacher said that the sun rises in the east.
options.feedback: Rises is correct: a general truth keeps the present simple even after a past reporting verb.

questions.explanation:
General truths are not backshifted, so the present simple rises stays unchanged in the report.

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the statement I saw Maria at the market?
questions.context: A witness reports what a neighbour said about a market.

options.text: Tom said that he had seen Maria at the market.
options.feedback: Had seen is correct: the past simple saw backshifts to the past perfect.

options.text: Tom said that he saw Maria at the market.
options.feedback: Saw keeps the simple past and does not show that the action is earlier than the report.

options.text: Tom said that he has seen Maria at the market.
options.feedback: Has seen mixes a present perfect with a past reporting verb.

options.text: Tom said that he sees Maria at the market.
options.feedback: Sees keeps the present simple and ignores the backshift.

questions.explanation:
After a past reporting verb the simple past saw becomes the past perfect had seen.

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the statement You should rest more?
questions.context: A patient repeats the advice given by a doctor.

options.text: The doctor told me that I shall rest more.
options.feedback: Shall is a different modal and does not match the original should.

options.text: The doctor told me that I should rest more.
options.feedback: Should is correct: the modal should has no past form and stays unchanged.

options.text: The doctor told me that I will rest more.
options.feedback: Will changes the meaning from advice to a future prediction.

options.text: The doctor told me that I would rest more.
options.feedback: Would changes should into a conditional form that the original does not have.

questions.explanation:
Modals such as should keep the same form in reported speech because they have no past tense.

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the statement I will lend you my car?
questions.context: A brother repeats a promise about a car.

options.text: Ana told me she will lend me my car.
options.feedback: Will keeps the present modal and my does not change to her.

options.text: Ana told me she would lend me my car.
options.feedback: Would is right but the possessive my must become her in the report.

options.text: Ana told me she would lend me her car.
options.feedback: Would and her are correct: will backshifts to would and the possessive my becomes her.

options.text: Ana told me I would lend her my car.
options.feedback: The pronouns are reversed: Ana is the lender and I am the receiver.

questions.explanation:
The report changes will to would and adjusts both pronouns: she would lend me her car.

questions.context: A listener reports what a friend said about a missed call.

options.text: He said he had already left when I called.
options.feedback: Had left is correct: the past perfect stays past perfect, and you becomes I for the listener.

options.feedback: Has left changes the past perfect into a present perfect.

options.text: He said he would already leave when I called.
options.feedback: Would leave turns a completed action into a conditional one.

questions.statement: Which direct statement is the source of Tom said that he had been working all morning?
questions.context: A student matches a reported sentence with the words it comes from.

options.text: I am working all morning, Tom said.
options.feedback: Am working would backshift to was working, not to had been working.

options.text: I have been working all morning, Tom said.
options.feedback: Have been working is correct: the present perfect continuous backshifts to the past perfect continuous.

options.text: I worked all morning, Tom said.
options.feedback: Worked would backshift to had worked, a simple past perfect without the continuous idea.

options.feedback: Will work would backshift to would work, a future form, not a perfect continuous.

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the statement I will meet you here tomorrow?
questions.context: A girl repeats what a friend said about a meeting place and day.

options.text: He said he will meet me here tomorrow.
options.feedback: Will, here and tomorrow all stay in the original viewpoint.

options.text: He said he would meet me here tomorrow.
options.feedback: Would is right but here and tomorrow are not adjusted for the report.

options.text: He said he would meet me there the next day.

options.feedback: Would is right but yesterday reverses the meaning of tomorrow.

questions.context: A boy repeats what his sister said about their brother.

options.feedback: Does not know and is keep both verbs in the present, so no backshift happens.

options.text: Laura told me she did not know where her brother is.
options.feedback: Did not know is right, but the verb is in the second clause must also backshift to was.

options.text: Laura told me she does not know where her brother was.

options.text: Laura told me she did not know where her brother was.
options.feedback: Both clauses backshift and the possessive changes: did not know and was, with her for my.

questions.explanation:
Every verb in the reported clause backshifts, so the sentence needs did not know and was, plus her.
